subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and own a runtime-agnostic agent-core protocol for no-Node or bare-metal ports, or keep those ports external until a narrower plugin/SDK seam is requested?
rationale: The remaining work is an architecture and product-scope choice across core runtime, Gateway protocol, plugin SDK, platform adapters, and external ports; source inspection confirms it is not an already-defined bug fix.

options.title: Sponsor Protocol RFC
options.body: Define the runtime-neutral agent-core schemas, lifecycle, conformance tests, and reference boundary before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Keep External For Now
options.body: Leave MimiClaw-style ports outside core/ClawHub until they identify a concrete missing OpenClaw API rather than a full runtime split.

options.title: Narrow To Plugin ABI
options.body: Route near-term work to JSON-RPC or agent-harness plugin APIs while explicitly deferring bare-metal OpenClaw runtime ownership.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Protocol RFC
recommendation.body: Define the runtime-neutral agent-core schemas, lifecycle, conformance tests, and reference boundary before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest owner signal across the host runtime guard, agent-harness seam, install/runtime docs, and prior issue review.
